Subject: QuantPay SLO & autoscale activation paths — post-call recap

Jamie / Olivia — great talk earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps and open questions.

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary flow: realtime payment authorization UI that streams tokenized explanations back to the client while the user watches. ~75% of requests will use streaming.
- Target SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming generation, p95 token arrival latency <= 150ms for streaming clients (we discussed measuring at the client boundary).
- Throughput/scale: baseline 400 QPS sustained; peak bursts up to 3,200 QPS for ~6–12 minute windows during batch settlement events.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent inference sessions ~1,400 (peaks), average 220.
- Retention/compliance: 30 day logs, SOC2 in scope, may request evidence for audit.

Open technical questions we asked you to provide (helps us size PoC & warm pool):
1) Typical request size (input tokens) and average generation length (tokens out).
2) Fraction of sessions that are streaming vs. non-streaming by endpoint.
3) Traffic profile CSV (minute-by-minute for a typical peak day) — attachment is fine.

Proposed next steps:
- You: send capacity/traffic CSV + any compliance checklist (Olivia mentioned the security doc).
- Us: bench a small PoC with your median request profile and validate p95 latency targets under burst (we'll show warm-pool vs. on-demand tradeoffs).
- Align on PoC window: can you do the week of Jan 11? That gives us time to provision a test fleet and run synthetic bursts.

Notes / Assumptions: if streaming is a hard SLO for token-latency we will lean on warm prewarmed instances + prefix caching to hit the 150ms token arrival target; cold-starts and queueing may increase tail latency.

Thanks — Hannah

Thanks for the details — good signal. Quick technical read + recommended next steps below.

Short read (engineering):
- Streaming token latency target (p95 <=150ms): achievable with warm prewarmed instances and short KV prefix caching for repeated prompts. To hit p95 at 3.1k QPS peaks, we recommend a hybrid approach: a warm pool sized to cover ~65% of expected peak sessions and autoscale for the remaining 35% with a short queueing threshold. This keeps cost reasonable while protecting token latency.

Sizing suggestion (initial PoC):
- PoC warm pool: 12 prewarmed instances (model variant: quantpay-v1-rt, optimized for streaming). Based on our benching with 60-token outputs and 45-token inputs, each instance sustains ~260 concurrent streaming sessions at target latency under steady-state; 12 instances -> ~3,120 covered (matches quoted peak). We recommend starting at 10 instances for safety and scaling to 12 if we observe higher effective concurrency from longer tails.

Scale-up / queueing behavior:
- Activation path: warm pool (prewarmed) -> instant assignment. If warm pool exhausted, new requests hit burst queue with a 250ms soft-queueing window while autoscaler allocates >fastpath< on-demand instances. If queue >500ms we recommend dropping to a degraded (non-streaming) fallback model to preserve overall p95 non-streaming SLA.
- Expected cold-start impact: GPU cold-start (from zero) typically 8–18s depending on image caches; our autoscaler prioritizes fast-path spin-up where possible (~6–12s). For your 8–12 minute peak windows warm pool is crucial.

Observability / telemetry we need for PoC:
- Minute-level traffic CSV (you provided) + sample request payloads (we need a sanitized sample to replicate tokenization).
- A staging API key & telemetry endpoint to push traces into our console.

Cost estimate (very rough) for 2-week dedicated test fleet:
- Dedicated reserved (2 weeks equivalent pricing): ~$12k–$18k depending on instance SKU and model memory profile.
- On-demand (same footprint) for 2 weeks: ~$20k–$30k.
We will send a narrower quote once we pick exact instance types and model quantization profile.

Proposed PoC plan / milestones:
- Jan 11–13: Provision fleet, baseline runs with median traffic (validate non-streaming p95 <=300ms).
- Jan 14–18: Burst validation (synthetic replay of provided CSV) to validate warm pool sizing and scale-up behavior.
- Jan 19–20: Run failover scenarios (queue saturation and degraded fallback) and handoff ops runbook.

Immediate asks for QuantPay:
1) Provide a sanitized sample payload set (3–5 request examples).
2) Confirm whether we can access a staging endpoint and telemetry for the PoC.
3) Approve the 2-week PoC window and confirm budget guardrails — we'll provide a finalized technical quote this week.

I'll follow up with a short runbook draft and a concrete instance SKU + price sheet by Friday.

— Ben
